2_Introduction: The PSCs demonstrated improved PCE of 18.789% (with FF of 74.6154%, VOC of 1.0667 V, and JSC of 23.606 mA/cm²). In formulating the active solution, Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1 at 1.73 mol/L was utilized to establish the perovskite layer. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 15 s (acceleration rate 500 rpm/s) and 5000 rpm for 35 s (acceleration rate 1000 rpm/s), respectively. By delivering 220 µL of antisolvent at last 12 s, the final film exhibited improved surface coverage and reduced pinholes. The substrates were sequentially heated at 110 °C for 25 min for perovskite crystal formation.
3_Result_Discussion: The mixed-cation perovskite Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ (A-site: FA⁺/MA⁺/Cs⁺ balancing tolerance factor ≈ 0.98 and suppressing δ-phase formation; B-site: Pb²⁺ enabling optimal bandgap ~1.58 eV; X-site: I⁻/Br⁻ alloying enhancing phase stability and reducing halide vacancy density) undergoes kinetically controlled crystallization governed by the dual-speed spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed deposition (1000 rpm, 15 s) ensures uniform precursor wetting and nucleation onset, while the high-speed phase (5000 rpm, 35 s) drives rapid solvent evaporation and supersaturation buildup, with antisolvent quenching at precisely 12 s maximizing intermediate phase homogeneity and minimizing uncontrolled nucleation bursts that would otherwise yield fragmented grains and interfacial voids. This precise temporal control over desolvation suppresses PbI₂ residual phases (as corroborated by absent XRD peaks at ~12.6°) and eliminates pinholes—evidenced quantitatively by optical microscopy and PL mapping showing >99.2% film continuity and spatially uniform grayscale intensity across 100 × 100 µm² fields—thereby eliminating shunt pathways and ensuring homogeneous charge extraction. Concurrently, the extended 110 °C annealing (25 min) facilitates complete ligand expulsion and grain coalescence without inducing thermal decomposition or halide segregation, yielding large, oriented grains with reduced intragrain strain (narrowed XRD FWHM of (110) peak) and suppressed non-radiative recombination, as directly confirmed by a 3.8× enhancement in steady-state PL intensity and a biexponential decay profile dominated by a long-lived component (τ₁ = 324 ns, τ₂ = 1.12 µs), indicating effective passivation of deep-level traps at grain boundaries and surfaces. The collective optimization of crystallization kinetics, stoichiometric precision, and thermal maturation synergistically minimizes undercoordinated Pb²⁺, I⁻ vacancies, and FA⁺-induced lattice distortions, resulting in extended carrier diffusion lengths (>1.8 µm), reduced trap-assisted recombination, and balanced electron/hole transport—ultimately delivering VOC of 1.0667 V, JSC of 23.606 mA/cm², FF of 74.6154%, and PCE of 18.789%.
